title: Emotional Preferences as Goal-Priority Regulation
abstract: arXiv:2608.27072v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: A core question in decision-making for agents is whether the relative priorities of competing lower-level objectives can be determined by emotional preferences autonomously generated by higher-level goals, rather than being externally prespecified. Under changing external environments and evolving internal states, emotions play an important functional role in regulating the relative priorities of competing goals. Inspired by the goal-directed theory of emotion, this paper studies how such preference regulation can be computationally realized through reinforcement learning. translated_title: 情绪偏好作为目标优先级调节机制
translated_abstract: 一个关于智能体决策的核心问题是，竞争性低层目标的相对优先级是否能由高层目标自主生成的情绪偏好来决定，而非由外部预先指定。在不断变化的外部环境和不断演化的内部状态下，情绪在调节竞争性目标的相对优先级方面发挥着重要的功能性作用。受情绪的目标导向理论启发，本文研究了如何通过强化学习在计算上实现这种偏好调节。我们首先提出了一种涌现性情绪偏好的概念：一个高层目标自主地诱导出对竞争性低层目标的、状态依赖的偏好。这一概念构建在一个由多目标强化学习内控制器和外偏好生成器组成的框架之上。内控制器提供了一套偏好库。
tldr: 本文提出了一种通过强化学习实现高层目标自主生成情绪偏好以动态调节竞争性目标优先级的新框架。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a novel framework that uses reinforcement learning to enable high-level goals to autonomously generate emotional preferences for dynamically regulating the priorities of competing objectives.
